title: Configure Vercel KV environment variables
description:
The backend KV migration is complete but Vercel KV environment variables are not configured in production.

Error in console:
@vercel/kv: Missing required environment variables KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN

Steps to fix:
1. Go to Vercel dashboard: https://vercel.com/
2. Select uffp-backend project
3. Go to Storage tab
4. Create a new KV database (or connect existing)
5. Copy the environment variables
6. Go to Settings > Environment Variables
7. Add KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN
8. Redeploy

Impact: Blocks uffp_mobile-87u deployment
notes:
Final fix deployed - added ioredis adapter for Redis URLs with credentials.

@vercel/kv doesn't support URLs with embedded credentials (username:password in URL).
Created redis-client.ts adapter that uses ioredis for generic Redis URLs.

Verification steps:
1. Wait ~2 minutes for deployment
2. Refresh app at https://uffpmobile.vercel.app/
3. Create forecast: /question Will AMD reach 00 in 2025?
4. Console should show: 'Created forecast on backend' with ID
5. NO errors about credentials or KV

This should FINALLY work!

Ready for verification.
close_reason: Fixed: Configured ioredis adapter to handle REDIS_URL with embedded credentials. Backend now successfully persists forecasts to Redis.

title: Forecasts being created with local IDs instead of backend IDs
description: Forecasts are being created with local IDs (e.g., 1769844910687-...) instead of backend IDs. This means when we try to add drivers, the backend returns 'Forecast not found'. Need to debug why backend forecast creation is failing or falling back to local.
notes: Added enhanced logging to debug backend forecast creation. Code changes include request data logging, full response logging, and detailed error info. Waiting for Vercel deployment to test.

title: Backend addDriver API returning 500 error
description: When trying to add a driver to a forecast, the backend API /api/forecasts?action=addDriver returns 500 Internal Server Error. This prevents drivers from being synced to the backend. Forecast ID: 1769844910687-...

title: Cannot simulate local-only forecasts
description:
Old forecasts created with local-only IDs (e.g., 1769844910607) cannot be simulated because they don't exist on backend. Backend returns 404 when trying to simulate.

Possible solutions:
1. Add migration to push old local forecasts to backend
2. Add UI indicator showing which forecasts are local-only vs backend-synced  
3. Allow local-only simulation for forecasts without backend IDs
4. Add /migrate command to push current forecast to backend

Current workaround: Create new forecasts with /question after backend sync is enabled.

title: Backend using in-memory storage - data lost on restart
description:
CRITICAL: Backend database.ts uses in-memory Map storage which loses all data when Vercel serverless functions restart (which happens frequently).

Current code:
const forecasts = new Map<string, Forecast>();

This causes:
- Forecasts created successfully but lost minutes later
- 'Forecast not found' errors when adding drivers
- Complete data loss on each deployment

Solution: Migrate to persistent storage:
1. Vercel KV (Redis) - recommended for serverless
2. Vercel Postgres
3. Supabase
4. Any persistent database

Impact: P0 - blocks all backend functionality
notes:
Fix deployed to production.

Migrated from in-memory Map storage to Vercel KV (Redis) for persistent storage.

Verification steps:
1. Create a new forecast with /question
2. Check console - should see backend create logs
3. Wait 5 minutes (or trigger new deploy)
4. Add a driver to the forecast
5. Should NOT get 'Forecast not found' error

Expected: Forecasts persist across serverless function restarts and drivers can be added successfully.

Ready for verification by human.
